missing.status: Synthetic method demonstration; not empirical project results
missing.assumptions: Seed 20261006; 180 fictional events; deaths and injuries are incomplete. Missingness depends only on the observed reporting index (MAR by construction). Five independently initialized chains run 20 iterations of fully conditional specification with five-donor predictive mean matching. Conditional predictions use log1p counts. This small Python demonstration is not output from the R mice package or the study.

climate.status: Synthetic method demonstration; not empirical project results
climate.assumptions: Assumed trajectories: m(t) = 0.06t or 0.14t; envelope half-width = 0.015t + 0.001t². Envelopes are illustrative ranges, not fitted confidence intervals.

flood.status: Synthetic method demonstration; not empirical project results
flood.assumptions: Twelve equally weighted, fictional communities. The empirical cumulative distribution is the share with travel time ≤ t. Both route scenarios are assumed, not measured Nepal–China travel times.

food.status: Synthetic method demonstration; not empirical project results
food.assumptions: Synthetic response function: p = logistic(−3 + 4c + 2a + 3ca). Conflict c runs 0–1; access restriction a is 0.2 or 0.8. Coefficients are assumed—not fitted food-insecurity effects.

aid.status: Synthetic method demonstration; not empirical project results
aid.assumptions: Assume independent Poisson events. Rate = events / worker-months × 1,000; log-Wald interval = rate × exp(±1.96/√events). These are method examples, not estimates of aid-worker risk.

weights.status: Synthetic method demonstration; not empirical project results
weights.assumptions: Three fictional cases. Score(w) = w × accessibility + (1 − w) × oversight gap. Both inputs are assumed 0–1 indices; no weapons capabilities or transfers are modeled.

decision.status: Synthetic method demonstration; not empirical project results
decision.assumptions: Three normal distributions with the listed means and standard deviations. The final column is the normal probability of a positive change. No posterior or fitted empirical model is claimed.
